Border(less) is a research proof of concept for one engineering question: can a phone keep choosing the best of several network servers continuously while spending as little energy as possible on that choice? The app answers it in practice: servers are checked only when a check can pay off, checks ride along with traffic the phone sends anyway, scans stop as soon as the answer is known, and every decision's cost is measured on the device itself (CPU time, radio time, battery current) and shown in the statistics.

It is a personal technical experiment, published as is, without any warranty and without any service behind it: it ships no servers and connects only to the servers its user adds. It is not an advertisement and does not promote any means or ways of network access: it offers, sells or distributes no servers, subscriptions or access to them, and calls on no one to use such means. Use it only in line with the laws and the network rules that apply to you.

Supporting a link format is interoperability, not an endorsement. The app reads the links its user already has — including wdtt:// and qwdtt:// links (WDTT and WDTT Plus) — and nothing more: it does not create, host, operate, sell or distribute such servers, credentials or access to them, is not affiliated with WDTT or WDTT Plus, and includes none of their software. Such a link is a set of credentials for a server run by someone else: using it means trusting that operator and following that service's rules. Any server you add stays your own choice and responsibility, as does using the app within the law and the rules of the networks it connects to.

A faster server must also gain at least this many milliseconds: both minimums must be met

Some kinds of connection tend to break more often once in use, so here they count as slower: XHTTP that sends everything in one stream (stream-one, stream-up, “auto” with Reality) 1.5× + 100 ms (it can stall on large uploads while pings pass); UDP transports (Hysteria2, WireGuard, mKCP, XHTTP over HTTP/3) 1.3× + 80 ms; everything in one connection (gRPC, mux) 1.2× + 50 ms, one lost packet holds up all of it; Shadowsocks without a wrapper 1.2×; TLS without a browser fingerprint 1.1× + 30 ms. Together at most 2× + 200 ms. They are still used when nothing better answers.
